title: Projective chart versus cone: numerical bound and tangent-generator equality
statement:
Let $k$ be any field, let $r\geq0$, and give $B=k[X_0,\ldots,X_r]$ its total-degree grading [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Let $C\subseteq B_+=(X_0,\ldots,X_r)$ be a homogeneous ideal and put $S=B/C$. Let $\mathfrak p\subset k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ be a prime ideal containing $f(1,t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ for every homogeneous $f\in C$. Set
$$Q=k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]_{\mathfrak p},\qquad J=(f(1,t_1,\ldots,t_r):f\in C\text{ homogeneous})Q,\qquad F=Q/J,$$
with maximal ideals $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak n$ of $Q$ and $F$ respectively [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $L=Q/\mathfrak q$ and $\delta=\operatorname{trdeg}_k L$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Define $h_F(n)=\operatorname{length}_F(F/\mathfrak n^{n+1})$, $h_S(n)=\sum_{j=0}^n\dim_k S_j$ and $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{j=0}^n f(j)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Then $Q$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] and
$$ (\Lambda^{\delta+1}h_F)(n)\leq h_S(n)\quad(n\geq0).$$
Define $\nu_B(C)$ to contain $d\geq1$ with multiplicity $\dim_k(C_d/\sum_{j=1}^d B_jC_{d-j})$, sorted increasingly and padded by infinitely many $\infty$'s. If $\Lambda^{\delta+1}h_F=h_S$, then $\nu^*(Q,J)=\nu_B(C)$.
For a regular local ring $(W,\mathfrak l,\kappa)$ and an ideal $\mathfrak c\subseteq\mathfrak l$, write $E(W,\mathfrak c)=\ker(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l}W\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l/\mathfrak c}(W/\mathfrak c))$. The sequence $\nu^*(W,\mathfrak c)$ contains $d\geq1$ with multiplicity $\dim_\kappa(E_d/\sum_{j=1}^d(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l}W)_jE_{d-j})$, sorted increasingly and padded by infinitely many $\infty$'s.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), Lemma 8, pp.160--162; (9.1)--(9.6), pp.162--164; Propositions 10--11 and Lemma 12, pp.164--167; second part of Remark (12.2), pp.167--168. Read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this complete comparison.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring], $Q$ is Noetherian regular local. First handle a rational point, over an arbitrary field $K$: write its coordinates as $(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$, replace $X_j$ by $U_j=X_j-a_jX_0$, and put $u_j=t_j-a_j$. This invertible linear homogeneous substitution preserves each quotient dimension and each minimal-generator multiplicity. The chart ring is $K[u]_{(u)}$, its residue field is $K$, and its maximal ideal is generated by the $u_j$. Modulo $(u)^{n+1}$ every denominator $b$ with $b(0)\ne0$ has the polynomial inverse $b(0)^{-1}\sum_{i=0}^n(1-b/b(0))^i$. Thus the truncated local polynomial ring is exactly $K[u]/(u)^{n+1}$; its monomials of degree at most $n$ are a basis.

source.place: Lemma 8, pp.160--161, rational chart and truncated-polynomial model; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text: In these rational coordinates dehomogenization $X_0=1,U_j=u_j$ identifies $B_n$ with polynomials in $u$ of degree at most $n$. Composing with the quotient to $F/\mathfrak n^{n+1}$ is surjective and kills $C_n$. Therefore $\dim_K S_n\ge h_F(n)$. Here length equals $K$-dimension: a monomial-degree filtration of the truncated quotient has subquotients annihilated by $(u)$, and refining each by a vector-space basis gives a composition series; any strict submodule inclusion increases vector-space dimension. Summing the inequality through $n$ proves $\Lambda h_F\le h_S$. This also proves all lengths used here are finite.

source.place: Lemma 8(i), p.161; jet surjection in the reverse (quotient) formulation; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text: Suppose equality holds in this rational case. Subtract the equalities at $n$ and $n-1$ (use zero for the sum at $-1$) to obtain $\dim_KS_n=h_F(n)$ for every $n$. Consequently the image of $C_n$ in $K[u]/(u)^{n+1}$ is the entire kernel of the quotient to $F/\mathfrak n^{n+1}$. For homogeneous $f\in C_d$, let $f(1,u)=g_m(u)+\cdots+g_d(u)$, with $g_j$ homogeneous and $g_m\ne0$. Its $m$-jet lies in that kernel. The unique degree-$m$ homogenization of this jet is $g_m(U)$, so $g_m(U)\in C_m$. Subtract $X_0^{d-m}g_m(U)$ from $f$ and repeat with the next nonzero component. There are at most $d+1$ components. Hence, for $G=K[U_1,\ldots,U_r]$ and $H=C\cap G$, one has $C=HB$ and $J=H K[u]_{(u)}$. No degree-zero component can occur, since evaluation at the point kills $C$.

source.place: Lemma 8(iii), pp.161--162; explicit homogeneous-component elimination; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text:
The degree-$d$ monomials identify $\operatorname{gr}_{(u)}K[u]_{(u)}$ with $K[U]$: independence follows by multiplying a proposed relation by its denominator and taking its lowest-degree part, whose scalar factor is the nonzero constant term of that denominator. Under this identification $E(Q,J)=H$. Indeed $a/b\in J$, with $b(0)
e0$, can be represented with $a\in H$; its initial form is the lowest homogeneous part of $a$ divided by $b(0)$, and belongs to the homogeneous ideal $H$. Conversely every homogeneous element of $H$ is such an initial form. Finally $C/(B_+C)=H/(G_+H)$ degree by degree: evaluate $X_0=0$ on $HB=H[X_0]$, so all terms divisible by $X_0$ disappear. Thus the multiplicities defining $
u_B(C)$ and $
u^*(Q,J)$ agree. This proves the equality assertion for rational points, including $H=0$ and $r=0$.

source.place: Lemma 8(iii), p.162; polynomial extension and tangent-ideal identification; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text: Return to the original $k$ and put $a_j=\bar t_j\in L$. Fraction evaluation gives $L=k(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$: the image of $k[t]/\mathfrak p$ generates its fraction field, the residue field of $Q$. Put $k_i=k(a_1,\ldots,a_i)$, $\mathfrak p_i=\ker(k_i[t]\to L)$, $Q_i=k_i[t]_{\mathfrak p_i}$, $C_i=Ck_i[X]$ and $F_i=Q_i/J_i$, with $J_i$ the dehomogenized ideal. Thus $Q_0=Q$, $F_0=F$, and $Q_r$ is the rational-point local ring over $L$. The fraction map $(k_i\otimes_{k_{i-1}}Q_{i-1})_{\ker(\mathrm{evaluation})}\to Q_i$, $a\otimes(b/s)\mapsto ab/s$, is an isomorphism: its inverse sends each coefficient and each $t_j$ to the corresponding element and inverts exactly the elements with nonzero evaluation. It carries the extended ideal to $J_i$. Each $Q_i$ is regular local by the polynomial-ring leaf. Apply [lem-trf-simple-residue-extension-hilbert-comparison] to get $\Lambda^{e_i}h_{F_{i-1}}\le h_{F_i}$, where $e_i=\operatorname{trdeg}_{k_{i-1}}k_i\in\{0,1\}$. The tower formula [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower] gives $\sum_i e_i=\delta$.

source.place: (9.1)--(9.6), pp.162--164; successive coefficient-field extensions at the chosen residue point; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text:
Scalar extension of finite-dimensional vector spaces preserves dimensions and quotients: extend a basis of a subspace to a basis of the ambient space. Applied in each degree to $C_i\subset k_i[X]$, and to the subspace $\sum_{j=1}^d B_jC_{d-j}\subset C_d$, this shows that $h_{S_i}=h_S$ and $
u_{k_i[X]}(C_i)=
u_B(C)$. Summation preserves inequalities, so Step 5 and the rational inequality give $\Lambda^{\delta+1}h_F\le\Lambda h_{F_r}\le h_S$. If the endpoints are equal, every inequality in this chain, including each summed extension inequality, is equality. To check the latter assertion without cancellation assumptions, a positive gap at index $n$ in any intermediate comparison remains positive at that same index under every subsequent summation; it would give a positive endpoint gap. Hence $h_{F_i}=\Lambda^{e_i}h_{F_{i-1}}$ for every $i$. The equality clause of [lem-trf-simple-residue-extension-hilbert-comparison] gives $
u^*(Q_{i-1},J_{i-1})=
u^*(Q_i,J_i)$. Step 4 at the final rational point and the scalar-extension multiplicities then give $
u^*(Q,J)=
u_B(C)$, as required. For $r=0$ the tower is empty and the rational calculation applies directly.

source.place: Remark (12.2), pp.167--168; equality propagated through the finite extension chain; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

I read all 6 steps and the new node in full. Step 1: the polynomial-ring leaf gives that Q and every Q_i are regular local. The coordinate shift and the inverse of a denominator modulo (u)^{n+1} are correct. Step 2: dehomogenisation maps B_n bijectively onto K[u]/(u)^{n+1} and onto F/n^{n+1}, killing C_n. Step 3: equality in every degree, then the lowest-component elimination, gives C=HB and J=HQ. Step 4: initial forms give E(Q,J)=H, and C/B_+C equals H/G_+H. Step 5: (k_i⊗Q_{i-1})_{ker ε} is identified with Q_i (localisation commutes with tensor). The trdeg tower leaf gives the sum of the e_i as δ. Step 6: a positive gap survives Λ, which forces every intermediate equality; scalar extension leaves h_S and ν_B unchanged. Item tests: C=0 gives equality; a linear point gives equality with ν=(1^r); C=(X_1^2) gives equality with ν=(2); an embedded vertex component and the conic X_0^2+X_1^2 over ℝ give strict inequality; r=0 is fine.
